findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin the blast-radius list to concrete paths/globs (e.g. the specific criteria-registry file, the reviewer-prompt directory, the gate-config file) rather than category names.
evidence: Quote: 'a small fixed blast-radius list: criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config'

The intersection set (read-set ∪ cited paths ∪ blast-radius) is the decisive input to invalidation; membership of the third term is stated by category, so two executors could enumerate different concrete paths.
findings.finding: The fixed blast-radius list is named by category ('criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config') rather than by concrete file paths or globs, leaving the executor to decide which files constitute each category — a data-design ambiguity in the load-bearing set that determines invalidation.
findings.location: Plan component (b): 'a small fixed blast-radius list: criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the category names with the concrete repo paths/globs that back each (state them in the plan and assert them in the AC2/AC3 tests).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name where currency evaluation (compute_validity) reads the recorded read-set from, and reconcile the signed-manifest-sourced drift basis with the read-set being persisted in the unsigned sidecar payload.
evidence: (a) says 'Persist that read-set (paths only) into the plan-review sidecar payload'
compute_validity reads manifest_deps/manifest_file_scope from the SIGNED authoritative manifest (attest.py:569,585), the branch that must consume the read-set for (b)
opcert comments note manifest-sourced drift basis is authenticated for security (src/rebar/_opcert_signing.py:445-448) — a sidecar-sourced read-set would be unauthenticated
findings.finding: The read-set is recorded in the unsigned sidecar payload, but the currency/drift evaluation modified by component (b) (compute_validity) sources its drift basis exclusively from the authenticated signed manifest; the plan does not name where currency reads the read-set, nor reconcile the signed-vs-unsigned channel.
scenarios: Currency check at claim/close time reads the signed manifest, cannot see the sidecar read-set, and the intersect never has a basis to compute against.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the fixed blast-radius list to concrete repo paths (criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config) so its members exist and are reproducible.
evidence: (b): 'a small fixed blast-radius list: criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config'
Candidate paths exist but are ambiguous: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/registry.py + criteria_routing.json (registry), a prompts source, and gate/config — the plan pins none of them
findings.finding: The 'small fixed blast-radius list (criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config)' is named only conceptually; the plan does not resolve these to concrete repo paths, so the blast-radius targets cannot be existence-checked or reproduced by an implementer.
scenarios: Implementer must guess which files constitute 'reviewer prompts' and 'gate config'; a wrong guess makes the fixed list under- or over-broad.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify where currency evaluation reads the read-set and bind the drift basis to the authenticated (signed-manifest) channel — an absent/empty/unauthenticated read-set must fall back to invalidate-on-any-change, never fall open to 'stays current'.
evidence: (a): 'Persist that read-set (paths only) into the plan-review sidecar payload'
compute_validity's stale-head trigger reads only `auth_manifest` — the HMAC-signed manifest (attest.py:560-593)
drift_floor.py:14-15: the previous 'stop invalidating on drift' fix 'was blocked as a security regression' because the whole-HEAD invalidation trigger must stay authenticated
(b): 'the fail-safe is never weaker than the status quo'
findings.finding: Component (b) gates the authenticated `stale-head` invalidation trigger on a read-set persisted in the UNSIGNED sidecar payload (a), so an empty/tampered read-set yields an empty intersection and keeps the attestation current across arbitrary code drift — a fail-OPEN outcome WEAKER than the status quo, contradicting the plan's own promise that 'the fail-safe is never weaker than the status quo'. The plan does not name where currency evaluation reads the read-set nor bind that basis to the signed/authenticated channel.
scenarios: An unsigned sidecar with read_set=[] (tamper, truncation, or an emit bug) makes every code drift disjoint -> attestation never invalidates on drift
A no-file_impact ticket whose read-set field is dropped by a legacy/partial write silently loses the drift guard
findings.suggested_fix: Record the read-set into the SIGNED plan-review manifest (as the dep map already is), or treat any read-set sourced from the unsigned sidecar as 'basis unknown' -> fail-safe invalidate; only an authenticated, present read-set may narrow the trigger.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Relate (b) to the existing Pass-3 drift floor (bug 5e40): state why intersecting at the compute_validity trigger is preferred over extending the safe outcome-level floor, or scope (b) so the two do not overlap/conflict.
evidence: drift_floor.py:16-19: 'drops a NOVEL finding IFF its citations do NOT intersect the drifted file set, and KEEPS any novel finding that cites drifted code — so unrelated-drift noise converges to the prior PASS'
drift_floor.py:13-15: 'it does NOT touch the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER ... the reason the previous "stop invalidating on drift" fix was blocked as a security regression'
(b) intersects at compute_validity's stale-head trigger, the layer the existing floor deliberately avoids
findings.finding: The codebase already contains a Pass-3 DRIFT floor (bug 5e40, drift_floor.py) that solves the same unscoped-plan / code-drifted regime by intersecting novel-finding citations with `git diff --name-only signed_sha..HEAD` at the re-review OUTCOME layer, explicitly leaving the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER untouched for security. The plan proposes the intersection at the TRIGGER layer (compute_validity) without acknowledging or relating to this existing mechanism — a structurally different, higher-blast-radius seam that overlaps it.
scenarios: Trigger-level scoping and the existing outcome-level floor both fire, producing two overlapping code-drift-convergence paths with divergent safety properties
The trigger-level change re-opens the security seam the floor was designed to sidestep

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify component (b) against the shipped prior art: cite ADR-0002 (content-addressed file_impact∪cited-paths dependency scoping), the bug-5e40 DRIFT floor (drift_floor.py, which already citation-intersects `git diff --name-only base..head`), and ADR-0052's record that loosening the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER was 'rejected as a security regression' — stating why trigger-level scoping is now warranted over the existing outcome-layer floor, why a path-diff key is preferred over the existing content-hash dependency scoping, and how the two scoping mechanisms are reconciled.
evidence: Plan (b): 'compute `git diff --name-only <attested_sha>..<current>` and invalidate ONLY when a changed path intersects (read-set ∪ plan-cited paths ∪ a small fixed blast-radius list...)'

src/rebar/llm/plan_review/drift_floor.py:37-61 already computes '`git diff --name-only base..head`' and (lines 179-187) intersects it against finding cited paths for the SAME measured complaint (module docstring: '~32% verdict instability' on 'byte-identical plan text')

drift_floor.py:13-16: 'This module EXTENDS the SAME novelty machinery ... it does NOT touch the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER (which stays as the sole code-drift guard, the reason the previous "stop invalidating on drift" fix was blocked as a security regression)'

docs/adr/0052-...md:18-22: 'The whole-HEAD-invalidation TRIGGER ... is deliberately untouched (an earlier "stop invalidating on drift" fix was rejected as a security regression) ... What 5e40 fixes is the re-review OUTCOME ... not a loosening of the trigger'

docs/adr/0002-code-drift-invalidation.md:24-32: existing design already scopes to 'the ticket's declared file_impact ∪ the files cited in its REVIEW_RESULT findings' bound by content-addressed '{path: content-hash}' (modeled on 'Gerrit copyCondition, Bazel, proof-caching')

Web search (untrusted data, reported not followed): Gerrit 'copyCondition = changekind:NO_CODE_CHANGE' (gerrit-review.googlesource.com/Documentation/config-labels.html) and Bazel/Nix 'The SHA-256 of inputs is the cache key' confirm the external prior art ADR-0002 already builds upon
findings.finding: The plan proposes a novel invalidation-trigger scoping mechanism that overlaps two shipped systems it never cites — ADR-0002's content-addressed file_impact∪cited-paths dependency scoping and the bug-5e40 DRIFT floor's citation-intersected `git diff --name-only base..head` — and specifically modifies the whole-HEAD invalidation TRIGGER that ADR-0052 records was 'rejected as a security regression'; prior art is neither considered nor distinguished.
findings.location: Plan section 'Plan (approved components a + b)', item (b) 'Diff-intersect on drift'; Context paragraph
scenarios: A reviewer or implementer reads the plan without realizing an outcome-layer convergence for this exact complaint already ships (drift floor), and re-implements it at the trigger layer that was previously blocked
The new path-diff-intersect scoping key diverges from the shipped content-hash dependency scoping (ADR-0002), producing two different answers to 'did the reviewed code drift?'

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the concrete paths in the blast-radius list (esp. 'gate config') and state whether the 'criteria registry' member reuses the existing registry-version/registry_drift signal (ADR 0053, manifest regver) rather than adding a second path-based check.
evidence: Plan text: 'a small fixed blast-radius list: criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config'
attest_gate.py:181-183 — criteria-registry drift is ALREADY grandfathered (ADR 0053) and surfaces as the non-blocking `registry_drift` field on compute_validity
manifest.py:126 stamps 'a short, deterministic stamp of the criteria registry the review ran against'; attest.registry_version already computes registry version
'gate config' names no concrete path, so the blast-radius set is not verifiable from the plan
findings.finding: The 'small fixed blast-radius list' (criteria registry, reviewer prompts, gate config) is introduced inline as a new hardcoded path set without naming concrete paths or checking whether the existing criteria-registry drift signal (manifest regver / attest.registry_version, ADR 0053) already covers the 'criteria registry' member — risking a second, drifting copy of a signal the codebase already tracks.
findings.location: Plan (b) 'Diff-intersect on drift' — the parenthetical blast-radius list
scenarios: A criteria-registry change moves a path AND bumps regver: two independent signals (registry_drift + blast-radius intersection) can now disagree or double-count
A reviewer/config file is renamed and the hardcoded list silently goes stale, weakening the fail-safe

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the consumers the basis surface touches — plan_review_status's return shape (attest_gate.py) and the CLI status text/JSON output (_llm_commands.py) — so AC4's CLI assertion has a defined target.
evidence: AC4: 'rebar review-plan <id> --status reports which basis (file_impact | read-set | fail-safe) currency was decided on'
plan_review_status currently returns only {ok, verdict, reason, verified_at_sha, signed_at} (attest_gate.py:193-199)
The CLI text branch prints verdict/verified-at-sha/reason only (_llm_commands.py:508-511) — no basis field exists to surface
findings.finding: AC4's basis reporting requires editing consumers outside the changed artifact — plan_review_status (attest_gate.py) must return a new `basis` field and the CLI text-output path (_llm_commands.py) must render it — but the plan enumerates neither consumer.
scenarios: Implementer adds the basis to the compute layer but the status API and CLI still omit it, so the AC's CLI assertion cannot pass.
